storage: git-versioned keyed JSON datacore/eia/weekly_series.json — WHOLE-FILE REBUILD per run (the source serves full history every pull; git history keeps vintages and EIA revisions surface as diffs), NOT append-only
written_by: scripts/eia_weekly.py (Python, session-run ~weekly; never on Railway — see cot.json _note on envelope-test coverage of Python writers)
source: EIA dnav hist_xls weekly series (keyless; all five endpoints probed 2026-07-05)
license: US government work, public domain; attribution 'U.S. Energy Information Administration'

field_map.series.<key>.title_as_published: the series title READ FROM THE SHEET — a moved/renamed upstream series shows as a title diff, never silent mislabeling
field_map.series.<key>.points: [[iso_date, value], ...] full weekly history; gaps are SKIPPED, never zero
field_map.selection: crude_stocks_us (ex-SPR), gasoline_stocks_us, distillate_stocks_us, spr_crude_stocks, natgas_working_l48 — Cushing deliberately NOT duplicated (the tank-fill EIA comparator owns it)

confidence_model: RAW official weekly estimates as published; EIA revises occasionally — the rebuild-plus-git-history model captures revisions as diffs rather than a vintage column (stated trade-off, same as railep724). All-series failure refuses to write; partial failure writes what succeeded and prints the failures.
started: 2026-07-05 (history to 1982-08-20 captured in the first build)
cadence: source updates Wednesdays (petroleum) / Thursdays (natgas); session-run refresh ~weekly
_note: Universal archive envelope (approved 2026-07-04). BUILD ORDER 3 #2; hypothesis (storage-vs-seasonal-band deltas condition the energy regime) stays gate-locked — archive only.
